captions.instagram:
"Go S corp" is common advice. The payroll part usually gets skipped.

✔️ As a sole owner or partner, you pay 15.3% self-employment tax on 92.35% of your net profit.
✔️ As an S corp owner who works in the business, the IRS expects a reasonable salary before any distributions. That salary carries payroll taxes; distributions above it don't.
✔️ New costs come with it: a payroll service, a Form 1120-S return and, in some states, extra fees.

Whether it pays off depends on your profit and those costs. Run your numbers on our S corp calculator, or book a call and we'll look at them with you.
